remedy.notes: The fabricated citations sat in the trial court’s own signed order, but the opinion states that order was largely prepared by the prosecutor as a proposed order, and the AI use is entirely prosecutor-side; the trial judge was neither sanctioned nor found to have used AI. Recorded here as prosecutor-side conduct that contaminated an adjudicative document, not as adjudicator-side AI use. No product named — the opinion says only “artificial intelligence software”. Footnote 4 preserves separate State Bar and Judicial Qualifications Commission proceedings, so a later disciplinary phase is possible. Two justices concurred in part and dissented in part, objecting only to admonishing the district attorney’s office. Official caption spells the appellant “Hannah Renea Payne”.
